final.title: Measure email threading before you automate it
final.body:
If you are thinking about email threading, treat it as a workflow decision first, not a software feature. The useful question is simple: are replies hard to follow, is context split across inboxes, or do follow-ups drift far enough that work gets repeated? If it is only occasional annoyance, automation is probably not the right place to spend attention. A cleaner mailbox habit may be enough.

The practical next step is manual. Review one week of email activity and mark every thread that went off track because the context was missing or hard to reconstruct. Note what caused the break, how long it took to recover, and whether the same problem shows up again. That gives you a real measure of the cost before anyone reaches for tools.

If the issue keeps repeating, the bounded decision is whether your existing email or CRM setup needs better configuration, or whether the workflow is specific enough to justify a small AI-assisted pilot for categorisation or routing. Keep that pilot narrow and keep human approval in place for any high-risk step. No need to turn every inbox wobble into a project; email already has enough drama.

final.title: Measure email threading before you automate it
final.body:
If you are thinking about email threading, start with one bounded workflow decision: is the problem worth fixing at all? For a small business owner, the real issue is not whether inbox software has a threading feature. It is whether lost context, duplicate replies, or missed follow-ups are happening often enough to justify changing the workflow.

The practical next step is manual. Review one week of email activity and mark every thread that went off track because the context was hard to follow. Note what happened, how long it took to recover, and whether the same problem shows up again. That gives you a real picture of the cost before anyone reaches for automation. No need to turn every inbox wobble into a grand plan.

If the problem keeps repeating, the next decision is still bounded: either configure your existing email or CRM setup better, or consider a small AI-assisted pilot for categorisation or routing. Keep the scope narrow and keep human approval in place for any high-risk step. Do not use it for bulk email or other sensitive correspondence.
